page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Configured with 2 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz and a single thread per core, the instance eliminates hyperthreading contention. It provides 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, along with hardware AES encryption support. The instance includes a 6 Gbps baseline network interface, provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and features no local NVMe storage or discrete GPU acceleration, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent disk storage.

Benchmark evaluations highlight respectable single-threaded execution offset by aggregate throughput limitations inherent to a 2-core envelope. Single-threaded performance sits in the average tier, demonstrated by a 1,807.0 Geekbench single-core score, a 1,707.18 single-core stress-ng metric, and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression measuring 14.15 GB/sec. Memory operations show capable bandwidth, posting 56.91 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and an average PassMark memory score of 2,529.89. Conversely, multi-threaded capabilities fall into lower quartiles due to core count constraints, seen in a 3,224.0 multi-core Geekbench score, 30.28 GB/sec gzip compression, and 4.54 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an efficiency perspective, r8gn.large delivers high memory allocation per compute unit on energy-efficient Graviton hardware, minimizing operational overhead for RAM-bound tasks without requiring excessive vCPU provisioning. The primary tradeoff stems from the absence of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage bandwidth management for disk-heavy tasks. The instance is well-suited for lightweight database deployments, in-memory caching tiers such as small Redis and Memcached nodes, memory-intensive backend services, and intermediate ETL workers that need ample RAM but moderate processing capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 16.0 GB of memory to yield an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 36 MB of L3 cache, 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies entirely on remote EBS storage, featuring zero bundled local NVMe capacity and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the platform demonstrates solid single-threaded metrics, achieving average Geekbench single-core results and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput. However, its overall multi-threaded throughput and integer processing are constrained by the 2-core footprint. Delivering high memory density per core, the r8gn.large offers a cost-effective operational profile for memory-intensive caching tiers, small in-memory key-value stores like Redis, and lightweight database applications that prioritize memory capacity over dense multi-threaded compute.
